scenario: AITA for being home all day and refusing to cook for my mom? | I'm a female in my senior year of high school and I have a younger sister in grade 10. As most of you know, schools have been closed for a while now and won't reopen for at least another month. My dad gets to work from home, but my mom still has to go out to her office. My school just started online teaching, and we've been getting a lot of assignments to complete. However, my mom expects us to make dinner basically every night because "we're home all day". That really annoyed me because yeah "we're home all day" but we have school work to do. I got upset and asked her why doesn't she cook, since she always finishes work at 5 pm and her office is like 6 minutes from home. Well, once she got home today and saw there was no dinner prepared, she got pissed and started screaming at me how she's so ashamed of us and how we're useless. When I explained how yes we're home all day but doesn't mean we have the whole day off, she got even more mad and said that it doesn't take that long to cook. I refuted by "why don't you cook then?" For more context, my mom is an awful cook. She literally puts no effort into learning or looking up recipes. My dad is an excellent cook. He's tried to teach her before, but she refuses to learn and complains. Before, he would cook for us almost every day, even if he came home late from work (he has a high demanding job so his hours range but he's home 6 pm the EARLIEST, sometimes as late as 9 or even 10 pm. + 30-40 minutes one way commuting). And what does he come home to? Either a low effort flavourless meal from my mom, or my mom sitting on her ass watching TV and asking him what's he's gonna make for dinner. So my dad is forced to make dinner at a late hour so he can eat. More recently, he would just eat fast-food before coming home because he doesn't expect dinner to be on the table. However, he asks if us girls are hungry and offers to cook something for us to eat because he's worried that our mom didn't make us a proper meal. I'm a good cook too (self taught), and I try to help out if I don't have too much homework to do. I did a lot of the cooking during the first 3 weeks before online school started, as well as baking lots of treats like breads, cookies, meringues etc. Also, my dad does practically all the chores in the house, while my mom spends all her time sitting on her ass watching TV. So AITA for not cooking dinner today and telling my mom to not expect dinner every time she comes home? Also, my dad ended cooking in the end today.

Here’s a breakdown of the key issues and why your response might be justified in some ways but also requires nuance: ### **Key Points to Consider:** 1. **Unequal Distribution of Labor** - Your mom expects you and your sister to cook while she goes to work, but she doesn’t contribute to dinner prep herself. This is unfair, especially since she’s the one who leaves the house and has the time to cook (she finishes at 5 PM, while you’re still doing schoolwork). - Your dad does most of the cooking and chores, which is also unfair. If he’s the one who cooks most nights, why should you and your sister be expected to take over? 2. **Your Mom’s Poor Cooking Skills** - If she’s a bad cook and refuses to learn, it’s unreasonable to expect you to cook for her. She should either: - Learn to cook properly (even if it’s just simple meals). - Hire help (if possible). - Accept that she can’t cook and rely on others (like your dad) to do it. 3. **Schoolwork vs. Housework** - You’re in high school with heavy assignments, and your sister is in 10th grade. Cooking every night is an unreasonable expectation when you’re supposed to be focusing on schoolwork. If your mom can’t cook, she should either: - Cook during the day (when she’s at work, she could prep meals). - Accept that you can’t cook every night and find another solution. 4. **Your Dad’s Role** - He’s the one who usually cooks, but he’s also the one who’s exhausted from work. If he’s already doing most of the cooking, it’s not fair to expect you to take over. He should be the one helping with dinner, not you. 5. **Your Mom’s Reaction** - She got angry and called you "useless," which is unfair. If she’s the one who’s not contributing, she shouldn’t blame you for not doing her job. ### **Was It Right or Wrong to Refuse?** - **Not wrong, but not the best approach.** - You were justified in saying, *"Why don’t you cook?"* because she’s the one who’s supposed to be doing it. - However, **passive resistance (not cooking and letting your dad do it)** isn’t the best solution. Instead, you could have: - **Firmly said:** *"Mom, we have schoolwork to do. If you can’t cook, then you need to figure out a solution—either learn to cook or hire help."* - **Suggested a compromise:** *"Can we take turns cooking, or can you prep meals during the day so we don’t have to cook every night?"* ### **Why Your Mom Reacted Poorly** - She’s likely used to you and your sister doing the cooking, and she’s not used to being held accountable. Her reaction shows that she’s not taking responsibility for her own actions. - If she’s ashamed of you, it’s because she’s not setting a good example. If she expects dinner every night, she needs to either cook or pay for it. ### **Final Verdict: <1> (Not AITA, but the situation is unfair and needs to change)** - You weren’t *wrong* for refusing to cook, but you could have handled it better by being more direct and demanding change. - The real issue is that your mom isn’t taking responsibility for her own role in the household. She needs to either cook or accept that she can’t and find another solution. Would you like help drafting a script for talking to your mom about this?
